methodological_rigor.justification: Competent WES methodology with rigorous quality control (Q30>97%, MQ≥30, PCR duplication <5%) and validation via Sanger sequencing. Population-based study includes 60 PRSCC cases with clear criteria. However, the WES analysis is limited to a single tumor case, which severely restricts the ability to confirm whether identified mutations are recurrent features or patient-specific, and limits generalizability. Authors explicitly acknowledge this critical limitation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: PRSCC is a rare, aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis (median survival 9.9 months) and clear clinical need. Study identifies potential prognostic marker (T stage as independent OS predictor) and proposes HYDIN as immunotherapy target. However, translational pathway is speculative—functional mechanisms are proposed but not experimentally validated in PRSCC models. Clinical impact remains theoretical without validation in larger cohorts.

reporting_quality.justification: WES methodology comprehensively described with specific tool versions and parameters; population study clearly detailed with inclusion/exclusion criteria; limitations section appropriately acknowledges constraints. IHC and Sanger methods well documented. However, no mention of public data deposition (WES files, processed data, or analysis code) in recognized repositories. REMARK biomarker standard mostly followed but data sharing incomplete.

novelty_literature.justification: First whole-exome sequencing study in PRSCC, identifying novel HYDIN A/G variant (Chr16:70908736) never previously reported in this malignancy. Characterizes 10 driver genes and 8 predisposing genes specific to PRSCC pathogenesis. While HYDIN mutations are known in other cancers, their identification and role in PRSCC fills a significant gap in the genomic landscape of this rare neuroendocrine tumor.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion); appropriate use of technical terminology for oncology audience; informative figures (Circos plots, rainfall/kataegis analysis, oncoplot) and comprehensive tables; Discussion balances findings with limitations and future directions; writing is precise and organized.

key_strengths: First WES study characterizing the genomic landscape of PRSCC, identifying a novel HYDIN driver mutation with immunotherapeutic potential
Rigorous WES methodology with high-quality control metrics (Q30>97%) and orthogonal validation via Sanger sequencing
Systematic literature review integrating 60 PRSCC cases from published studies identifies T stage as independent prognostic factor for overall survival
Comprehensive genomic analysis (SNVs, INDELs, CNVs, SVs) with functional pathway enrichment across RTK-Ras, NOTCH, and Wnt pathways
Thorough discussion of proposed mechanisms linking HYDIN mutations to poor prognosis via immune regulation and oncogenic pathway activation
key_concerns: Single-case WES analysis is the fundamental limitation; generalizability unknown without validation in larger PRSCC cohorts (authors propose 30-50 samples needed)

No functional validation of proposed mechanisms; all mechanistic hypotheses (immune evasion, JAK-STAT activation, Hedgehog pathway effects) are inferred from literature in other cancers, not demonstrated in PRSCC
WES data and processed genomic files not deposited in public repositories, limiting reproducibility and reuse
Therapeutic recommendations for HYDIN-targeted immunotherapy and pathway inhibitors lack experimental support in PRSCC-specific models or clinical evidence
Population-based study reliant on published literature introduces potential reporting and selection bias; follow-up times and treatment details incomplete in many cases
chief_reviewer.rationale: This competent but pilot-scale genomic study makes a novel discovery (HYDIN mutation) in an extremely rare malignancy where any characterized genetic data advances the field. However, the single-case design, lack of functional validation, and absence of public data sharing limit tier placement to 3. Major revisions would require prospective multi-center case collection and experimental validation of HYDIN-driven mechanisms before higher-tier publication.
